title_en: Banking Supervision Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of strengthening the supervision and administration of the banking industry, regulating supervisory and administrative acts, preventing and mitigating banking risks, protecting the lawful rights and interests of depositors and other customers, and promoting the sound development of the banking industry.

Article 2 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of banking financial institutions and their business activities within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
For the purposes of this Law, banking financial institutions mean financial institutions that absorb public deposits, such as commercial banks, urban credit cooperatives, rural credit cooperatives, and policy banks, which are established within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
The provisions of this Law on the supervision and administration of banking financial institutions shall apply to the supervision and administration of financial asset management companies, trust and investment companies, finance companies, financial leasing companies, and other financial institutions established within the territory of the People's Republic of China upon approval by the banking regulatory authority of the State Council.
The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law, exercise supervision and administration over the financial institutions established outside the territory of the People's Republic of China upon its approval, as well as the business activities of the financial institutions mentioned in the preceding two paragraphs outside the territory.

Article 3 The objectives of banking supervision and administration are to promote the lawful and sound operation of the banking industry and to maintain public confidence in the banking industry.
Banking supervision and administration shall protect fair competition in the banking industry and enhance the competitiveness of the banking industry.
Article 4 The banking regulatory authority shall, in exercising supervision and administration over the banking industry, follow the principles of lawfulness, openness, fairness, and efficiency.

Article 5 The banking regulatory authority and its staff engaged in supervision and administration shall perform their duties of supervision and administration according to law and shall be protected by law. Local governments, government departments at all levels, social organizations, and individuals shall not interfere.

Article 6 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall establish a mechanism for sharing supervisory and administrative information with the People's Bank of China and other financial regulatory authorities under the State Council.

Article 7 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council may establish mechanisms for supervisory and administrative cooperation with banking regulatory authorities of other countries or regions, and implement cross-border supervision and administration.

Article 8 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall establish local offices as needed for performing its duties. The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall exercise unified leadership and management over its local offices.
The local offices of the banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall, within the scope authorized by the banking regulatory authority of the State Council, perform their duties of supervision and administration.
Article 9 Personnel engaged in supervision and administration of the banking regulatory authority shall have the professional knowledge and work experience commensurate with their positions.

Article 10 Staff members of the banking regulatory authority shall be devoted to their duties, act according to law, be fair and honest, shall not take advantage of their positions to seek illegitimate benefits, and shall not hold concurrent positions in financial institutions or other enterprises.

Article 11 Staff members of the banking regulatory authority shall keep State secrets according to law and shall have the duty to keep secrets for the banking financial institutions and parties under their supervision and administration.
Where the banking regulatory authority of the State Council exchanges supervisory and administrative information with banking regulatory authorities of other countries or regions, it shall make arrangements for the confidentiality of such information.

Article 12 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall make public its supervisory and administrative procedures, and shall establish a system of responsibility for supervision and administration and an internal supervision system.

Article 13 Where the banking regulatory authority engages in such supervisory and administrative activities as handling risks of banking financial institutions and investigating and punishing related financial illegal acts, local governments and relevant departments at all levels shall provide cooperation and assistance.

Article 14 The auditing and supervisory authorities of the State Council shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws, supervise the activities of the banking regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 15 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall, in accordance with laws and administrative regulations, formulate and promulgate rules and regulations for the supervision and administration of banking financial institutions and their business activities.

Article 16 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall, in accordance with the conditions and procedures prescribed by laws and administrative regulations, examine and approve the establishment, change, termination, and business scope of banking financial institutions.

Article 17 Where an application is made for the establishment of a banking financial institution, or a banking financial institution changes its shareholders whose total capital contribution or total shareholding reaches or exceeds a prescribed proportion, the banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall examine the sources of funds, financial status, capital replenishment ability, and integrity of such shareholders.

Article 18 The business types within the business scope of a banking financial institution shall, in accordance with regulations, be subject to examination and approval by or filing with the banking regulatory authority of the State Council. The business types requiring examination and approval or filing shall be prescribed and published by the banking regulatory authority of the State Council in accordance with laws and administrative regulations.

Article 19 Without approval by the banking regulatory authority of the State Council, no entity or individual may establish a banking financial institution or engage in the business activities of a banking financial institution.

Article 20 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall implement qualification management for the directors and senior officers of banking financial institutions. The specific measures shall be formulated by the banking regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 21 The prudential operation rules for banking financial institutions shall be stipulated by laws and administrative regulations, and may also be formulated by the banking regulatory authority of the State Council in accordance with laws and administrative regulations.
The prudential operation rules specified in the preceding paragraph shall include risk management, internal control, capital adequacy ratio, asset quality, loss reserves, risk concentration, connected transactions, asset liquidity, and other matters.
Banking financial institutions shall strictly comply with the prudential operation rules.

Article 23 The banking regulatory authority shall conduct off-site supervision on the business activities and risk conditions of banking financial institutions, establish a supervisory information system for banking financial institutions, and analyze and evaluate the risk conditions of banking financial institutions.

Article 24 The banking regulatory authority shall conduct on-site inspections on the business activities and risk conditions of banking financial institutions.
The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall formulate on-site inspection procedures to regulate on-site inspection conduct.
Article 25 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall exercise consolidated supervision and management over banking financial institutions.

Article 26 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall, within thirty days from the date of receipt of a proposal from the People's Bank of China to inspect a banking financial institution, give a reply.

Article 27 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall establish a supervisory rating system and a risk warning mechanism for banking financial institutions, and shall determine the frequency, scope, and other measures to be taken for on-site inspections based on the rating status and risk conditions of banking financial institutions.

Article 28 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall establish a system of post responsibility for the detection and reporting of banking emergencies.
Where a banking regulatory authority discovers a possible emergency that may trigger systemic banking risks and seriously affect social stability, it shall immediately report to the person in charge of the banking regulatory authority of the State Council; if the person in charge of the banking regulatory authority of the State Council deems it necessary to report to the State Council, he or she shall immediately report to the State Council, and shall inform the People's Bank of China, the finance department of the State Council, and other relevant departments.

Article 29 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall, together with the People's Bank of China, the finance department of the State Council, and other relevant departments, establish a banking emergency response system, formulate contingency plans for banking emergencies, specify the responsible institutions and personnel and their duties, response measures and procedures, and handle banking emergencies in a timely and effective manner.

Article 30 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall be responsible for uniformly compiling statistical data and statements of banking financial institutions nationwide, and shall publish them in accordance with relevant state provisions.

Article 31 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall provide guidance and supervision over the activities of banking self-regulatory organizations.
The articles of association of banking self-regulatory organizations shall be filed with the banking regulatory authority of the State Council for record.
Article 32 The banking regulatory authority of the State Council may carry out international exchanges and cooperation activities related to banking supervision and management.

Article 33 The banking regulatory authority, as required for performing its duties, shall have the power to require banking financial institutions to submit, in accordance with regulations, balance sheets, income statements, and other financial accounting and statistical statements, operational management materials, and audit reports issued by certified public accountants.

Article 35 The banking regulatory authority may, as required for performing its duties, hold supervisory talks with the directors and senior officers of banking financial institutions, and require the directors and senior officers of banking financial institutions to provide explanations on major matters concerning the business activities and risk management of the banking financial institutions.

Article 36 The banking regulatory authority shall order banking financial institutions to faithfully disclose to the public, in accordance with regulations, information such as financial accounting reports, risk management status, changes in directors and senior officers, and other major matters.

Article 38 Where a banking financial institution has or may have a credit crisis that seriously affects the legitimate rights and interests of depositors and other customers, the banking regulatory authority of the State Council may, according to law, take over the banking financial institution or facilitate its reorganization, and the takeover or reorganization shall be carried out in accordance with relevant laws and the provisions of the State Council.

Article 39 Where a banking financial institution engages in illegal operation, poor operation and management, or other circumstances, and failure to revoke it would seriously harm the financial order and damage the public interest, the banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall have the power to revoke it.

Article 40 Where a banking financial institution is taken over, reorganized, or revoked, the banking regulatory authority of the State Council shall have the power to require the directors, senior officers, and other staff members of the banking financial institution to perform their duties in accordance with the requirements of the banking regulatory authority of the State Council.
During the period of takeover, reorganization, or liquidation upon revocation, with the approval of the person in charge of the banking regulatory authority of the State Council, the following measures may be taken against the directly responsible directors, senior officers, and other directly liable persons:
(1) If the departure from China of the directly responsible directors, senior officers, or other directly liable persons would cause significant losses to the national interest, notify the exit administration authority to prevent their departure according to law;
(2) Apply to the judicial authority to prohibit them from transferring or assigning their property, or from creating other rights over their property.

Article 41 With the approval of the State Council's banking regulatory authority or the head of its provincial-level agency, the banking regulatory authority shall have the power to inquire into the accounts of a banking financial institution suspected of financial illegality, its staff, and related actors; for suspected transfer or concealment of illegal funds, with the approval of the head of the banking regulatory authority, it may apply to a judicial authority for freezing.

Article 44 Where a banking financial institution is established without authorization, or the business activities of a banking financial institution are illegally engaged in, the State Council's banking regulatory authority shall ban such activities; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if no crime is constituted, the State Council's banking regulatory authority shall confiscate the illegal gains, and if the illegal gains are 500,000 yuan or more, a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains shall be imposed concurrently; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 500,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 47 Where a banking financial institution fails to provide statements, reports, or other documents or materials in accordance with regulations, the banking regulatory authority shall order rectification; if rectification is not made within the time limit, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 300,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 49 Where a person obstructs a staff member of the banking regulatory authority from performing duties of inspection or investigation according to law, the public security organ shall impose a public security penalty according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 50 Where laws and administrative regulations provide otherwise for the supervision and administration of policy banks and financial asset management companies established within the territory of the People's Republic of China, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 51 Where laws and administrative regulations provide otherwise for the supervision and administration of foreign-funded banking financial institutions, Sino-foreign equity joint venture banking financial institutions, and branches of foreign banking financial institutions established within the territory of the People's Republic of China, those provisions shall prevail.
Article 52 This Law shall come into force as of February 1, 2004.
